messages:
From: Rajiv Patel <r.rajiv@finapp.com>

Cc: security@finapp.com, Elena Morales <elena.m@finapp.com>

Subject: Request: redact prompts & outputs + serving logs (evidence)

Hi Marissa,

We're preparing for an audit window and must complete a targeted removal of prompt/input/response snapshots and related serving logs for a set of user IDs tied to our EU tenant. Specifically: all prompt text and model outputs for user_ids: [u-8342, u-9981, u-4402] between 2025-11-01 and 2026-04-30, plus any transient KV cache snapshots that persisted. Can you confirm Redwood's workflow for this — including how you produce deletion evidence we can include in our audit (manifest of deleted object keys, timestamps, and S3 object links or equivalents)?

We need a timeline and the absolute most minimal explainable proof to provide auditors (no content payloads, just hashes/keys + deletion timestamps). Also please call out any retention windows that would prevent deletion of logs older than X.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Head of Security, FinApp
security@finapp.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Patel <r.rajiv@finapp.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: redact prompts & outputs + serving logs (evidence)

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the clear ask. We're able to run a scoped removal for those user_ids; below is the proposed workflow and what we'll deliver for audit evidence. I want to make sure the plan matches your compliance expectations before we start.

Planned workflow (high level):
- Step 1: Freeze indexing on the FinApp tenant for the requested ID set (30 min maintenance window).
- Step 2: Run targeted scan across: prompt snapshots store, response cache, and short-lived serving logs.
- Step 3: Mark objects as scheduled-for-deletion and record object keys + content-hashes in a deletion_manifest.
- Step 4: Execute deletion from primary store (S3 or customer-dedicated volumes) and from warm caches; where immediate deletion cannot be guaranteed (immutable backup windows), we will schedule expiration and document retention hold windows.
- Step 5: Produce a deletion report (manifest CSV), signed metadata (timestamp, operator id), and S3 signed-delete links where available. We will also include SHA256 hashes of the deleted objects (not the content).

Deliverables (what you will receive):
- deletion_manifest_20260518.csv (keys, sha256, object_size_bytes, deletion_timestamp, storage_location)
- s3_deletion_links_20260518.txt (signed URLs to confirm objects were removed/refreshed; ephemeral)
- redaction_snapshot_20260518.png (screenshot of job run & job-id)
- short notes on any items deferred due to immutable backup windows or chained retention policies.

Timing: we can run the job Thursday 2026-05-14 02:00 - 04:00 UTC (recommended) and provide artifacts within 48 hours. If you need a different window, tell us.

Notes/constraints:
- Backup/archival retention: if any of the objects existed in offline archival copies managed under your account-level backup settings, Redwood can mark them and request expedited archival deletion, but can't bypass customer-managed immutable backups without a separate process and authorization.
- KV cache snapshots: short-lived caches will be purged; we will include a manifest of entries removed.

Please confirm and we'll schedule ops and a point-of-contact for the maintenance window.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Rajiv Patel <r.rajiv@finapp.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.m@finapp.com>, security@finapp.com
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: redact prompts & outputs + serving logs (evidence)

Marissa — confirmed. Thursday window works. Please include the following additional asks in the manifest: a column that lists whether the deleted object was also present in any replica region, and a short statement for each object whether the deletion was immediate or scheduled (and if scheduled, the scheduled expiry date). Also: we need a signed acknowledgement line from the Redwood operator who executes the job (name + employee id).

Can you cc Rishi and Monica on the run? I'll be watching the job and will expect the artifacts to land in the shared drive.

Thanks,
Rajiv

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Patel <r.rajiv@finapp.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 18 May 2026 17:28:00 -07:00
Subject: FINAPP: final deletion report and evidence artifacts (job id: run-20260518-09)

Rajiv / FinApp team — job run-20260518-09 completed at 2026-05-18T16:11:03Z. Summary below and artifacts are attached to this message and in the shared drive link we provided earlier.

Summary of execution:
- Scope: user_ids [u-8342, u-9981, u-4402], date range 2025-11-01 -> 2026-04-30
- Stores scanned: prompt_snapshots (s3://rw-prod-finapp/prompt_snapshots/), response_cache (ephemeral), serving_logs (s3://rw-prod-finapp/serving_logs/)
- Total objects removed: 1,278 (manifests attached).
- Replicated objects: 312 objects had replicas in eu-west-1; those replicas were deleted as part of the same job.
- Deferred items: 6 objects were in immutable backup with retention until 2026-06-02; those entries are flagged in the manifest and scheduled for auto-expiry on that date.

Artifacts delivered (attached):
- deletion_manifest_20260518.csv (contains object_key, sha256, size_bytes, deletion_timestamp, region_replica_flag, deletion_mode, operator_name, operator_id)
- s3_deletion_links_20260518.txt (signed verification links; valid for 72 hours)
- redaction_snapshot_20260518.png (screenshot of the run control panel and run-id)

Operator acknowledgement:
- Name: Rishi Malhotra
- Employee ID: RW-1053
- Execution timestamp: 2026-05-18T16:11:03Z
- Signed (internal audit token): audit-token-7a9c2b

Notes:
- The manifest includes a column deletion_mode with values: IMMEDIATE or SCHEDULED. SCHEDULED entries also show scheduled_expiry_iso in the CSV.
- We have not and will not include any content payloads in the artifacts; only object keys and hash digests are provided to satisfy auditability while preserving content confidentiality.

If you confirm acceptance of these artifacts, we'll mark the run as closed in our internal ticket and update your tenant's compliance log. If you need any additional attestations (e.g., SOC2-focused language), let us know and we can add a short attestation addendum.

— Rishi Malhotra
Infrastructure & Operations, Redwood Inference
